Recall that a linear congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ has a unique solution modulo $n$ if and only if $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$  

In the given congruence, we have $a=22$ and $n=31$, where

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(22,31)=1.
$$

So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $22\,(\text{mod}\,31).$ To find the inverse of $22\,(\text{mod}\,31)$, use the extended Euclidean algorithm. 

First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}31 & = & 22\cdot 1 & + & 9 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 22 & = & 9\cdot 2 & + & 4 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 9 & = & 4\cdot 2 & + & 1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving for the rightmost terms in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}9 & =31-22 \\ 4 & =22-9\cdot 2 \\ 1 & =9-4\cdot 2.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & =9-4\cdot 2 \\  & =9-(22-9\cdot 2)\cdot 2 \\  & =9\cdot 5-22\cdot 2 \\  & =(31-22)\cdot 5-22\cdot 2 \\  & =31\cdot 5-22\cdot 7 \\  & =31\cdot 5+22\cdot (-7)\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have 

$$
1=31\cdot 5+22\cdot (-7).
$$

We can write this result in modulo $31,$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}31\cdot 5+22\cdot (-7) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,31) \\ 22\cdot (-7) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,31) \\ 22\cdot (31-7) & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,31) \\ 22\cdot 24 & ≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,31)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $22\cdot 24≡1\,(\text{mod}\,31),$ which means that $24$ is the multiplicative inverse of $22$ (modulo $31$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our original congruence by $24,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}22x & ≡5 &  & (\text{mod}\,31) \\ 24\cdot 22x & ≡24\cdot 5 &  & (\text{mod}\,31) \\ (24\cdot 22)x & ≡120 &  & (\text{mod}\,31) \\ 1\cdot x & ≡3\cdot 31+27 &  & (\text{mod}\,31) \\ x & ≡27 &  & (\text{mod}\,31)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡27\,(\text{mod}\,31).$
